# Properties & Real Estate — sector digest, 2026-W46

**Coverage changes.** The desk ran the property batch across 11–12 November and published five names: PWON **BUY Rp312** and CTRA **BUY Rp615** (initiations, 11 Nov); JRPT **REDUCE Rp970** and CBDK **HOLD Rp2,816** (results updates, 12 Nov); MTLA **REDUCE Rp519** (initiation, 12 Nov; a text refresh is in QC). Both results updates moved the call the same day their initiation draft was signed: CBDK went SELL Rp1,582 to HOLD Rp2,816 once the land mark moved off 0.95x audited cost to a realised-ASP basis and the minority share of the mark-up was deducted; JRPT went HOLD Rp1,054 to REDUCE as the land mark and the sector discount band were applied. Sign-off returned CTRA, BSDE, MTLA and MKPI at least once, mostly on prose and valuation-arithmetic items.

**Deck moves.** There is no property deck; the property models read the macro deck, whose forecast path is unchanged this week (last reviewed 7 November). Only spot marks were refreshed: USD/IDR 18,190 on 13 November, BI rate held at 5.75%. No deck values changed.

**Material news.**
- `7e6863721fcc5981` (13 Nov): primary-market new-home sales fell 8.43% in Q3 2026.
- `ca327f5653628c71` (10 Nov): BI's Q3 2026 residential survey puts primary house prices up 0.58% while sales fell 8.43% — weak demand at higher prices.
- `1640cce4728bbab3` (11 Nov): the government set Rp394trn of programme credit for 2027, available for housing and business loans.
- `ce6fdb9748402de8` (12 Nov): MSCI's November rebalancing removes CTRA (with AVIA, MTEL, EMTK, JSMR, RAJA, WIFI) from the Global Small Cap indexes.

**What to watch.** Q4 and FY2026 marketing-sales prints in late January, the first test of whether the Q3 primary-sales contraction is stabilising; whether the 2027 subsidised credit lines reach housing demand; MSCI-related flows in CTRA; and the batch's shared inputs — five targets set on a near-identical 11.85–11.87% WACC and a common RNAV discount-and-roll convention, which the Sector Lead flagged at sign-off as the place to test for a sector-wide tilt.

*Research only; not a recommendation to act.*
